items.title: Trump Just Gave Canada Until January 1. If There’s No Deal, 50% Tariffs Hit Cars and Steel
items.summary: Trump's January 1 deadline gives GM and Ford just four months to rethink supply chains that took decades to build, and a little-known legal wrinkle could make the whole tariff structure collapse before either company finishes planning around it.

items.summary: Tesla just hiked Cybertruck prices on a vehicle that has been called the biggest flop in automotive history, and the reasoning behind that decision is nearly impossible to defend.

items.summary: Ford Motor is seeing a shift in how analysts frame its value as the Fair Value Estimate moves from US$14.85 to US$15.73. The change is coming as research firms reassess where the stock should trade, weighing wide ranging views on EV losses, the potential of Ford Energy, and how much to credit newer software and services. items.title: He Retired From Ford, Then Eyed Its $30,000 Electric Pickup. His Retiree Discount Suddenly Looked Uncomfortably Like Pay.
items.summary: A retired Ford assembly worker spotted the company's new electric pickup and remembered his retiree discount, then a familiar worry crept in: could saving money at a dealership cost him part of his Social Security check?

items.title: Fresh Tariffs Boost Domestic Steel, Dent Automakers
items.summary: Trade talks between the U.S. and Canada collapsed in the 11th hour Friday, renewing fears of an all-out trade war as new tariffs went into effect over the weekend. Ford and Stellantis shares slipped Monday after President Trump announced a 50% tariff on automobiles and auto parts from Canada come January.
